SMTO-CFG-0051 — SMTO can't start because its default database row count is too low

GUID: 8c54dcbf-32d4-4ef2-bfd7-0cbb6b1ddd38
Slug: config-database-default-limit-must-be-greater-than
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because the number of database rows it returns by default is set to zero or less. Your conversations and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find where SMTO is started (the terminal command, a startup script or the service settings) and look for a setting named AOR_DATABASE_DEFAULT_LIMIT. SMTO's default database row count comes only from that startup setting.
  2. Delete that setting to use SMTO's usual 100 rows, or change it to a positive whole number, such as 100. With a default of zero rows, database answers would always come back empty, so SMTO refuses the value.
  3. Start SMTO again from the same place where you changed the setting. The setting is read only when SMTO starts.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Leave the maximum database rows setting and other AOR_ settings unchanged; they are separate limits.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected database_default_limit (environment variable AOR_DATABASE_DEFAULT_LIMIT) because it is zero or negative.

What this means

  • database_default_limit is zero or negative during application settings validation. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • database_default_limit is zero or negative during application settings validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the default query limit separately from the maximum permitted rows.

How to fix it

  • Unset AOR_DATABASE_DEFAULT_LIMIT or set it to a positive integer (default 100) in the Server's launch environment, then restart. It is passed to the execution engine as database_default_limit and is separate from database_max_rows and sql.row_limit.
  • Set database_default_limit to a supported positive row count.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended positive default limit passes validation.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
